info.title: Crown API & Webhooks
info.description:
Open API 3 docs for Crown API

Webhook events that Crown will POST to your configured endpoint URL. All webhooks expect a 200 OK response. Payloads use kebab-case for all keys to match the Crown API conventions.

oneOf.description: Ethereum wallet address for source tokens (required only when source asset is a token like eth-mainnet/brlv, eth-base/brlv or eth-base/wbrly)

Ethereum wallet address for receiving tokens. Resolved server-side to an internal wallet, a whitelisted external wallet, or a target wallet. For FX (BRL<->USDC) orders, target wallets must also be FX-whitelisted for the account.

PIX key of a third-party end-user bank account to receive BRL. Allowed for USDC->BRL and BRLV->BRL orders. The recipient bank account's tax-id must match the tax-id registered on the account the order is executed on. When set, BRL is delivered directly to this PIX key; the API user's own bank account is not touched.

How the source BRL is collected. 'brcode' issues a one-time PIX QR for the exact amount that the account pays to fund a BRL->BRLV order; 'account-balance' funds from the account's existing BRL balance and is the default when this field is omitted.

signature.name: X-Crown-Signature
signature.description: HMAC-SHA256 signature of the request body using your webhook secret. Verify this signature to ensure the webhook is from Crown.

x-webhook-security.note: All webhook requests include an X-Crown-Signature header containing an HMAC-SHA256 signature of the request body. Use your webhook secret (provided when registering the webhook) to verify the signature and ensure the request is authentic.
verification-steps: 1. Extract the X-Crown-Signature header from the request
2. Compute HMAC-SHA256 of the raw request body using your webhook secret
3. Compare the computed signature with the header value
4. Only process the webhook if signatures match

example-code.python:
import hmac
import hashlib
import json

signature = hmac.new(
    webhook_secret.encode('utf-8'),
    json.dumps(request_body).encode('utf-8'),
    hashlib.sha256
).hexdigest()
is_valid = signature == request.headers['x-crown-signature']
